title: Cross-check weighting — independent second method (session arena/a8da1cca-korea8)

method.summary: Each provider is scored from four verifiable inputs — licence coverage, published adjacent evidence, published small-job fit and whether a written price is on file — then reduced for documented warnings. Higher scores rank first; ties are broken by the documented order below. This is an inquiry order, not a quality rating: no provider was contacted, no review score was verified, and no price was confirmed.

criteria.label: Licence coverage for a combined repair + restoration scope
criteria.rules: 3 = B and C-36 on the checked record; 2 = C-36 alone, or B with C-9; 1 = B or B-2 alone; 0 = no plumbing or building classification.

criteria.label: Published evidence of adjacent work
criteria.rules: 2 = company-published tub waste/overflow or ceiling-access case; 1 = company site advertises repair/bathroom plumbing; 0 = none verified.

criteria.label: Published fit for a small occupied-unit repair
criteria.rules: 1 = company publishes small-repair or residential occupied-property work; 0 = larger/commercial positioning or unconfirmed.

criteria.label: Written price on file for a removal/replacement scope
criteria.rules: 1 = owner-supplied amount whose stated scope includes removal/replacement of the assembly; 0 = no price, or an adjustment-only price.

tie_break: Written price on file for a removal/replacement scope
Holds C-36 (the trade of the failing part)
method.ceiling: Maximum possible score is 16 (3×3 + 2×2 + 1 + 2) before deductions.
method.exclusions: A suspended licence or an unresolved identity is excluded rather than scored.
method.limits: Scores use only what is published and verifiable. They say nothing about workmanship, insurance claims history, availability or price. Two firms with equal scores are effectively tied; the tie-break order is documented but arbitrary below the first three rules.
method.ties: Firms on equal scores are effectively tied; ranks 3–6 and 8–9 are within one tie-break step of each other and should not be over-read.

cost_rules.owner_amounts: The three supplied amounts are owner reports dated 2026-08-30 and are never presented as verified prices. Verified amounts stay blank.
cost_rules.permit_fee: Official San Francisco DBI fee schedule (July 2026): Category 1P $290, Category 11P/M $320, regular inspection $519/hour, off-hour inspection $555/hour, reinspection $259 per half hour. Category applicability for this job is unconfirmed.
cost_rules.fee_exemption: San Francisco Plumbing Code §104.5: replacement of a plumbing fixture without a change in drainage, piping or venting does not require payment of the permit issuance fee. Whether this job qualifies is unconfirmed.
cost_rules.no_totals: Owner-reported amounts and official fees are shown side by side, never summed. No total project cost is published.

rows.name: Rapid Flow Plumbing & Rooter
rows.why: Ranks first among the two combined-scope firms on the documented tie-break: the CSLB record holds both B and C-36, and the company's own site sells general contracting and plumbing across a simple-repair-to-renovation range. A Yelp-indexed account describes retrieving a tub drain plug through a wall opening; it is unverified and is not treated as proof of this job. Ace scores identically and is an equally reasonable first call.
rows.ask: Ask for a written scope covering: tub-side attempt first; below-ceiling fallback; who cuts and restores the ceiling; occupied-unit protection; permit position; current price. Confirm the licence is still current on signing day.

cost.cost_note: No price on file for this firm. If DBI Category 1P applies, the published fee is $290; §104.5 of the San Francisco Plumbing Code states that replacing a plumbing fixture without a change in drainage, piping or venting does not require payment of the permit issuance fee. Category applicability for this job is unconfirmed.
cost.total_note: Total unknown: no written price and no confirmed fee category.

rows.tie_note: Tied at 12 points with Ace Plumbing & Rooter (#2); the published one-contract combined offer breaks the tie.

rows.name: Ace Plumbing & Rooter
rows.why: Holds B, C-36 plus A, C-4, C-16 and C-10, carries workers'-compensation insurance and publishes residential plumbing work for HOAs and property managers. No published statement about tub overflow/trip-lever retrieval was verified, and the small-job fit is inferred from its residential service lines only.
rows.ask: Ask whether it self-performs drywall repair and texture, or names a licensed restoration subcontractor; request the same written scope and occupied-unit plan as above.

cost.cost_note: No price on file for this firm. If DBI Category 1P applies, the published fee is $290; §104.5 of the San Francisco Plumbing Code states that replacing a plumbing fixture without a change in drainage, piping or venting does not require payment of the permit issuance fee. Category applicability for this job is unconfirmed.
cost.total_note: Total unknown: no written price and no confirmed fee category.

rows.tie_note: Tied at 12 points with Rapid Flow (#1); no published one-contract combined statement.

rows.name: Expert Plumbing Solutions
rows.role: Plumbing specialist with a written price on file (C-36 only)
rows.why: The only supplied quote whose wording is closest to the actual failure — replace waste and overflow — so its owner-reported $614 is the most usable reference point in the file. The scope as supplied names no ceiling access, drywall restoration, permit or cleanup, and the licence is C-36 only.
rows.ask: Send back one identical scope and ask for a revised written price that separates plumbing from ceiling restoration; ask who performs the drywall work.

cost.cost_note: Owner-reported amount only; not independently verified. No ceiling/restoration line is included. If DBI Category 1P applies, the published fee is $290; §104.5 of the San Francisco Plumbing Code states that replacing a plumbing fixture without a change in drainage, piping or venting does not require payment of the permit issuance fee. Category applicability for this job is unconfirmed.
cost.total_note: Owner-reported $614 plus a conditional $290 fee would not be a verified total; the quote may exclude access and restoration.

rows.name: Heise’s Plumbing
rows.role: Plumbing specialist with adjacent case evidence (C-36 only)
rows.why: Has the strongest published adjacent evidence of any firm checked: company case studies of San Francisco tub waste-and-overflow replacements, one described as using ceiling access, and a site that says it handles jobs big or small. The licence is C-36 only (no B or C-9), so the ceiling repair must be performed or subcontracted by a properly licensed restoration party.
rows.ask: Ask directly whether they have replaced a stuck trip-lever/waste assembly through the ceiling, who closes and textures the opening, and whether they will contract the restoration or work alongside Bernal Hill.

cost.cost_note: No price on file. A ceiling opening adds a separate restoration cost that is not covered by a plumbing-only licence. If DBI Category 1P applies, the published fee is $290; §104.5 of the San Francisco Plumbing Code states that replacing a plumbing fixture without a change in drainage, piping or venting does not require payment of the permit issuance fee. Category applicability for this job is unconfirmed.
cost.total_note: Total unknown; two trades are likely to be invoiced.

rows.name: We Do Construction
rows.why: Holds B + C-36 and publicly offers self-performed plumbing inside one design-build contract, which is exactly the all-in-one structure this job needs. It is ranked below the specialists because its public positioning emphasises larger renovations, and no small occupied-unit repair acceptance or price is on file.
rows.ask: Ask whether the firm will take a small repair of this size, and get an itemised one-contract price that names the plumbing and the ceiling restoration separately.

cost.cost_note: No price on file. If DBI Category 1P applies, the published fee is $290; §104.5 of the San Francisco Plumbing Code states that replacing a plumbing fixture without a change in drainage, piping or venting does not require payment of the permit issuance fee. Category applicability for this job is unconfirmed.
cost.total_note: Total unknown; small-job acceptance itself is unconfirmed.

rows.why: A long-established B + C-36/C-4/C-16/C-20 licence that could lawfully hold a combined contract. Its own site describes a mechanical contractor for commercial building systems, so a small occupied-flat repair is outside its published positioning and no price is on file.
rows.ask: Ask whether it accepts a residential small repair and will name the restoration party; otherwise treat it as a fallback for the combined-contract structure only.

cost.cost_note: No price on file. rows.name: Bay Area Plumbing
rows.role: Plumbing specialist with a written price on file (C-36 only)

deductions.reason: Shares a street address and business phone with licence #749536 (Save-On-Interior); common ownership is not established

rows.why: Supplied an owner-reported $550 for the lever, plug and spout with diverter, labour and materials. That wording may describe a different assembly than the waste-and-overflow body, and the licence is C-36 only, so ceiling restoration is not covered. Its record shares an address and phone with another licence, which must be clarified before signing.
rows.ask: Ask which exact parts the $550 covers, who the contracting entity is, and who repairs the ceiling. Compare against Expert's $614 on one identical written scope.

cost.owner_reported_scope: Lever, plug and spout with diverter; labour and materials
cost.cost_note: Owner-reported amount only; scope wording may not match the failed assembly. If DBI Category 1P applies, the published fee is $290; §104.5 of the San Francisco Plumbing Code states that replacing a plumbing fixture without a change in drainage, piping or venting does not require payment of the permit issuance fee. Category applicability for this job is unconfirmed.
cost.total_note: Owner-reported $550 plus a conditional $290 fee would not be a verified total.

rows.name: Fast Response Plumbing & Rooter
rows.role: Plumbing specialist — adjustment quote only (C-36 only)
rows.why: The owner-reported $135 buys a repair or adjustment of the plunger handle, not removal of a stuck assembly or any ceiling access, so it does not rank as a replacement price. Licence is C-36 only. Its workers'-compensation policy expires 12/18/2026, which should be rechecked before work is scheduled.
rows.ask: Ask whether the handle can be freed without opening the wall and, if not, for a written replacement-plus-access price.

cost.cost_note: Owner-reported amount buys adjustment only; it is not a replacement or access price. If DBI Category 1P applies, the published fee is $290; §104.5 of the San Francisco Plumbing Code states that replacing a plumbing fixture without a change in drainage, piping or venting does not require payment of the permit issuance fee. Category applicability for this job is unconfirmed.
cost.total_note: A $135 adjustment is not comparable to the replacement quotes.

rows.name: Bernal Hill Drywall
rows.role: Restoration partner (C-9 + B) — pairs with a plumber
rows.why: The only checked firm holding C-9 drywall (plus B) with published patching, texture matching and small wall repairs. It cannot do the plumbing, so it is ranked as the restoration half of a two-party job rather than as a standalone hire.
rows.ask: Use it for the ceiling opening repair and texture, either as a named subcontractor on the plumber's contract or as a separate written contract with the plumbing scope clearly separated.

cost.cost_note: No price on file for the ceiling repair.
cost.total_note: Restoration cost is a separate unknown line.

note: This weighting was produced independently on 2026-11-08, before the canonical weighted ranking was merged. It uses four published inputs (licence coverage x3, adjacent published evidence x2, published small-job fit x1, written price x2, maximum 16) with deductions for complaint disclosure, future suspension and shared identity. It is published only as a cross-check on the canonical ranking, not as a second hiring list.
